What kind of legal agreements should co-parents create in order to establish custody and visitation rights?

Co-parents should create a parenting plan that outlines the shared parenting responsibilities, including custody and visitation rights. This plan should include:

5. Dispute resolution: This outlines the process for resolving any major disagreements between the co-parents regarding parenting.

Once the parenting plan is agreed upon, it can be submitted to the court for approval and become legally binding.

4. Resource centers: Many family resource centers offer workshops and classes on co-parenting and creating a parenting plan. These centers can provide you with information, guidance, and support as you navigate the process.

One way to ensure that your co-parent will follow the parenting plan is to have the plan incorporated into a court order. A court order can be obtained either through a court hearing or by submitting an agreement to the court for approval.

If your co-parent violates the terms of the parenting plan, you may be able to take legal action. Here are some steps you can take:

1. Communicate: Before taking legal action, try to communicate with your co-parent and address the violation. Bring up your concerns and try to work out a solution that can help maintain the integrity of the parenting plan.
